page: Microsoft Azure E96bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture and deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio intended for large memory footprints.

Storage architecture includes 5670 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside support for remote Premium Storage block volumes. The system does not incorporate GPU accelerators, concentrating physical platform resources entirely on memory capacity, CPU throughput, and high-speed local temporary disk space. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with this instance profile.

The instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive workloads where standard compute-to-memory ratios are insufficient and high-capacity temporary disk caching is essential. The allocation profile avoids overhead from unused accelerator hardware while provisioning substantial memory density. Primary target workloads include in-memory databases, large-scale data analytics, Redis caching clusters, and high-throughput transactional database engines requiring substantial local scratch storage.
